brand.subtitle: Knowledge Check — ESource WhiteLabel Sales Course

questions.question: What are the three main reasons firms buy the white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: Their brand, data stays home, and lower cost per client
Bank feeds, unlimited staff seats, and client login portal
Mobile app, payroll integration, and live transaction updates
Quick implementation, free training, and 24/7 support
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly right—these three reasons are the core value proposition and should be deliverable in one breath.
questions.feedback_incorrect: These are either competitor features or capabilities the tool doesn't yet offer. Review Slide 3 and the gaps mentioned on Slide 2 to see what we don't sell yet.

questions.question: What is the ideal firm size for the white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: Accounting firms with over 500 monthly clients
Bookkeeping and small CPA firms with roughly 5 to 100 monthly clients
Solo bookkeepers with 1 to 5 clients
Large national CPA networks with multiple offices
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—this is our best-fit customer profile, and it's important to start with the right firms.
questions.feedback_incorrect: Our sweet spot is mid-sized firms that want their own brand and value client privacy. Firms much larger or much smaller may not be a fit at this stage.

questions.question: According to the course, how should pricing be presented to firms?
choices: As final rates locked in for three years
As a flat fee per firm regardless of client count
As proposed pricing, with confirmation from Joe before anything is signed
As negotiable rates that vary by region
questions.feedback_correct: Right—always say 'proposed' and confirm with Joe, because the pricing tiers are still being finalized.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The course explicitly warns that pricing is proposed, not final. Always confirm final terms with Joe before any commitment is made.

questions.question: What does the reminder feature show in the demo, and why does it matter to bookkeepers?
choices: It reminds the bookkeeper to invoice clients monthly
It shows missing statements in red and allows texting the client from the bookkeeper's own phone, solving the monthly statement-chasing problem
It automatically files tax documents in the firm's cloud storage
It sends automated payroll reminders to the firm's accountant
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—this demo moment lands because chasing statements is a real monthly headache bookkeepers face.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The reminders feature specifically targets the pain of getting clients to submit statements. Review Slide 7 to see how this moment in the demo is staged and why it resonates.

questions.question: What should be included in the discovery questions before showing a demo?
choices: Ask about their marketing budget and office location
Ask about today's tools, cost pain, brand visibility, and time spent chasing transactions
Ask about their hiring plans and employee turnover
Ask about their revenue growth and tax filing deadlines
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—these four discovery questions uncover the specific pain points that your demo will solve.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The discovery phase is about understanding their current tools, cost challenges, brand concerns, and time drain. Write down answers in their own words so you can mirror them back during the demo.

questions.question: How are the pricing tiers structured for the white-label bookkeeping tool?
choices: One flat rate of $15 per client book for all firms
Graduated tiers where each band's rate applies only to books in that band: $20 first, $17 for 2–10, $15 for 11–30, $14 for 31–100, $13 for 100+
Tiered pricing based on the firm's annual revenue
A single per-seat cost multiplied by the number of staff
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—the graduated band structure is key, and it's important to explain that each rate applies only to books within that range.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The pricing is per active client book with graduated tiers, not per staff seat or per firm revenue. Review Slide 8 to see how to explain the band structure clearly.

questions.question: What is the most effective way to close a sale with a prospect?
choices: Ask them to switch all their clients at once to prove commitment
Propose a 3–5 client pilot for 60 days alongside their current system, with agreed success measures
Offer a one-time discount if they sign a multi-year contract
Require them to attend a full-day onboarding training before they can decide
questions.feedback_correct: Right—the pilot approach removes risk and lets both parties prove success before full adoption.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The pilot strategy is core to closing without resistance. A small test build confidence and demonstrates value before a big commitment.

questions.question: When a prospect says "Our clients know QuickBooks," how should you respond?
choices: Agree that QuickBooks is superior and suggest they stick with it
Explain that clients get Excel reports with the firm's name and don't need to learn any software
Offer free QuickBooks training to all their staff
Tell them QuickBooks is being discontinued anyway
questions.feedback_correct: Exactly—this response acknowledges the objection but shows clients don't interact with the software, only the reports.
questions.feedback_incorrect: This is a classic objection. The key is that clients receive reports with the firm's brand, not the software's brand, so they never need to learn the tool.

questions.question: Why is client data privacy a competitive advantage for the white-label tool compared to QuickBooks Online and Xero?
choices: It costs less to store data than QuickBooks
Client bank statements never leave the firm's computers, and books and backups are locked so only signed-in staff can access them
It includes a mobile app that competitors don't offer
It automatically files tax returns without leaving the firm
questions.feedback_correct: Perfect—data privacy and ownership is a powerful differentiator that no competitor can match at this level.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The privacy advantage is that client data stays on the firm's computers and is fully controlled by the firm owner. Review Slides 3 and 11 to understand the security and privacy story.

questions.question: According to the security story, what happens to the books on an employee's computer after the owner removes them from access?
choices: The books stay readable on their personal laptop so they can finish their work
The books are deleted immediately from all devices
At the next check-in, the books lock and become unreadable, even on a personal laptop
The employee can request a one-time access pass to retrieve their files
questions.feedback_correct: Correct—this automatic locking mechanism is the heart of the security story and reassures owners that client data stays secure.
questions.feedback_incorrect: The security design ensures that when an employee is removed, their access is revoked at the next device check-in, protecting client data from being taken. This is a key differentiator in the pitch.
